evidence.title: European Commission IP/26/1747, 26 Aug 2026: Statement of Objections over the proposed UPM/Sappi joint venture (read through trade-press and Concurrences summaries; the press-corner page itself returned only a header to the fetcher)
evidence.excerpt: The Commission's preliminary view is that the joint venture may restrict competition in the markets for communication paper. The concern named is that the JV would acquire market power allowing it to increase prices and decrease quality for customers of coated mechanical paper (magazine paper) and coated woodfree paper. Horizontal overlap only; no vertical or input-foreclosure theory is named. The parties may reply, examine the file and request an oral hearing.

evidence.title: PaperAge, 26 Aug 2026: UPM receives the Commission's Statement of Objections
evidence.excerpt: UPM calls the SO 'a customary step during an in-depth merger investigation' and says it 'is confident that it will be able to respond fully to the Commission's preliminary concerns'. 'Together with Sappi, UPM is reviewing the SO carefully' and 'will respond in due course', continuing to 'engage constructively with the Commission'. UPM maintains the JV is needed to 'secure reliable supply continuity for graphic paper customers in Europe'. No Sappi statement of its own in the piece; no...

evidence.title: Lesprom, 26 Aug 2026: UPM receives the statement of objections over the Sappi joint venture
evidence.excerpt: Reports the step and the parties' intention to respond; names graphic paper and the European graphic paper industry as the affected market. No Sappi statement quoted, no deadline given and no prediction that the venture will be blocked or abandoned.

evidence.title: Search-summary record, 8 Sep 2026: the decision deadline is 11 November 2026 and the JV is valued at EUR 1.42bn (MLex paywalled; Concurrences and the wood/paper trades carry the same)
evidence.excerpt: The Commission now has until 11 November 2026 to issue a final decision. The proposed 50-50 venture, valued at EUR 1.42bn, would combine the entire UPM Communication Papers business with Sappi's European graphic paper operations. MLex itself is paywalled to the fetcher; the deadline and the value come from the search summaries of MLex, Concurrences and the paper trades.

evidence.title: Pulp & Paper News, 3 Sep 2026: 'UPM-Sappi deal could weaken competition, EU warns' (page 403 to the fetcher; headline and framing from the search summary)
evidence.excerpt: The trade press reports the Commission's warning and the parties' response. Across PaperAge, Lesprom, Wood & Panel, Global Wood Markets and Pulp & Paper News, the framing is that the Commission has set out preliminary concerns and the parties will answer; none of them says the joint venture is likely to be blocked or abandoned.

evidence.title: UPM-Kymmene (HEL:UPM) daily closes, 21 Aug to 4 Sep 2026
evidence.excerpt: 24 Aug 23.94 (+1.14%); 25 Aug 23.79 (-0.63%); 26 Aug 23.76 (-0.13%); 27 Aug 23.84 (+0.34%); 28 Aug 24.00 (+0.67%); 31 Aug 24.06 (+0.25%); 1 Sep 24.27; 2 Sep 24.31; 3 Sep 24.01; 4 Sep 24.24. evidence.title: Sappi (JSE:SAP) daily closes, 21 Aug to 4 Sep 2026
evidence.excerpt: 21 Aug 1577 (+0.51%); 24 Aug 1509 (-4.31%); 25 Aug 1462 (-3.11%); 26 Aug 1440 (-1.50%); 27 Aug 1410 (-2.08%); 28 Aug 1447 (+2.62%); 31 Aug 1478 (+2.14%); 1 Sep 1390 (-5.95%); 2 Sep 1391; 3 Sep 1357 (-2.44%); 4 Sep 1360. Sappi was already falling before the objection (-4.3% and -3.1% on 24 and 25 August), and fell a further 1.5% and 2.1% on the 26th and 27th against UPM's -0.13% and +0.34%.

evidence.title: Coverage record, 8 Sep 2026: Sanoma closes not read; the customer-side leg is unverified
evidence.excerpt: The Sanoma history page returned 404 to the fetcher and no other free dated series for SAA1V was reached, so the customer-side call has no carrier reading. Mondadori and Elanders were not attempted. The Sappi side has no company statement of its own on the ledger either: SENS was not searched, and every report quotes UPM speaking for both parties.

resolutions.scorer_note: Early: the shape of the objection is stated and final. The concern named is market power to raise prices and cut quality for customers of coated mechanical and coated woodfree paper: a horizontal overlap between the two largest makers of the same product. No vertical or input-foreclosure theory appears in the release or in any of the coverage. The baseline said the same, so the row carries no edge.

The channel did not say it. PaperAge, Lesprom, Wood & Panel, Global Wood Markets and Pulp & Paper News all report the step and the parties' answer; none frames the venture as likely to be blocked or abandoned. The baseline (reports the step, quotes both parties, predicts nothing) had it. Narrative rows are scored on whether the channel spoke, never on whether it was right.

UPM -0.13% on the day of the objection, +0.34% and +0.67% on the next two sessions: no attributable move, far under the 3% falsifier, and no report attributes a move to the objection. The visibility ratio operated: a Phase II step on a business being carved out is small against the group. Baseline (the party falls on a regulatory setback) missed.

Sappi -1.50% and -2.08% on the two sessions from the objection against UPM -0.13% and +0.34%: the smaller party's relative move is the larger, as called. Stated confound: Sappi was already falling hard before the objection (-4.31% on 24 August, -3.11% on 25 August), so the level is not attributable to the event; the ordering claim is what was called and it holds.

The Sanoma series was not read: the history page returned 404 and no other free dated series was reached. The customer-side leg has no carrier reading at all, so the absence claim cannot be scored either way.

UPM confirmed publicly on the day and spoke for both parties ('Together with Sappi, UPM is reviewing the SO carefully'). No statement by Sappi in its own name was found; SENS was not searched. The claim was that both parties confirm, so one confirmed party and one unread carrier is unverified, not a hit.
